key_insight: A phenomenon-first LLM workflow can generate and screen qualitative materials hypotheses by separately framing guest physics, host capabilities, and operating context.
engineering_relevance: For materials discovery, this shifts LLM use upstream from solving a fixed task to proposing mechanistically distinct behaviors that can guide computational and experimental prioritization.
method: Decompose each case into guest, host, and operating-context prompts.
Ask the model to propose an unusual qualitative phenomenon plus mechanism, signature, and falsifier.
Repeat the workflow and compare against a guest-only baseline to assess breadth of mechanisms explored.
evidence_signal: Across 80 guest-host combinations, the model produced 57 proposals and nine computationally tractable candidates; structured formulation covered 21 broad mechanism families in both original and repeat runs versus eight for guest-only prompting.
watch_item: The approach still depends on careful curation and downstream feasibility checks, and many generated ideas are filtered out before validation.
paper_title: Phenomenon-first problem formulation with language models in metal-organic frameworks
